root_cause_summary: Three independent defects in the `caam monitor` probe, none of which indicate unhealthy accounts. (1) 401/"auth expired": monitor.Refresh() (internal/monitor/monitor.go:129) reads access tokens from vault profile copies via readAccessToken() (monitor.go:288) and never refreshes them; Claude OAuth access tokens expire in hours, and only the active profile's copy gets refreshed by live CLI spawns, so all non-active vault copies go stale and the usage endpoint returns 401/403, remapped to "auth expired (re-login)" by alerts.go shortUsageError(). The existing internal/refresh.RefreshProfile() already refreshes vault tokens in place and is the natural reuse point. (2) 429s: usage.MultiProfileFetcher.FetchAllProfiles() (internal/usage/multi.go:55-100) launches one goroutine per profile, sending 5 simultaneous GETs to api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage from one IP every 30s — a burst that trips provider rate limiting; 429 is then rendered as a fatal-looking WARN and the row's usage is discarded. (3) Codex "34% | unknown" WARN rows: the bar proves the fetch SUCCEEDED; "unknown" is authpool.PoolStatusUnknown.String() (profiles not enrolled in a pool — authpool/pool.go:144) rendered at render_table.go:71, and the [WARN] prefix is stale health-store status (healthEmoji at render_table.go:57) that ignores the just-successful fetch. Fix design: refresh-on-expiry/401 in the monitor probe reusing internal/refresh (per D2 leaning), serialized+spaced Claude fetches with Retry-After-aware 429 display that keeps last-known usage, and display fixes replacing meaningless pool-status/health noise with reset-time info.

beads.title: Epic: caam monitor shows false auth/usage errors for healthy accounts
beads.description_md:
# Epic: Fix false auth/usage errors in `caam monitor`

## User report (2026-07-03)
All accounts are HEALTHY (`caam shallow-spawn cc-cabot -- claude --dangerously-skip-permissions` comes up logged in with working /usage), yet `caam monitor` shows:

```
CLAUDE
[WARN] arthur@feta.fund     no usage: API error: status 429
[WARN] benson@feta.fund     no usage: auth expired (re-login)
[WARN] cabot@feta.fund      no usage: auth expired (re-login)
[WARN] saumil@feta.fund     no usage: API error: status 429
[WARN] saumil_2@feta.fund   no usage: auth expired (re-login)
CODEX
[WARN] arthur@feta.fund     ######--------------  34% | unknown
[WARN] saumil@feta.fund     ##########----------  54% | unknown
```

## Three root causes (all verified in code)
1. **Stale vault tokens** — `internal/monitor/monitor.go:288 readAccessToken()` reads access tokens from vault profile copies; `Refresh()` (monitor.go:129) never refreshes them. Only the active profile's tokens get refreshed by live CLI use. Non-active vault copies expire -> real 401/403 from `https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage` -> remapped to "auth expired (re-login)" by `shortUsageError()` in `internal/monitor/alerts.go:90-98`. Child bead: `monitor-refresh-stale-tokens`.
2. **Self-inflicted 429 burst** — `internal/usage/multi.go:55-100 FetchAllProfiles()` fires one goroutine per profile: 5 simultaneous GETs to the same endpoint from one IP, every 30s (default interval, monitor.go:88). 429 is rendered as a WARN error and usage discarded. Child bead: `monitor-429-pacing`.
3. **Cosmetic "unknown"/WARN noise on successful rows** — the Codex rows fetched real usage (the bar renders), but `render_table.go:71` appends `p.PoolStatus.String()` which is `"unknown"` for any profile not enrolled in an authpool (`internal/authpool/pool.go:135-144`), and the `[WARN]` prefix comes from stale health-store data (`render_table.go:57`, `monitor.go:318+ buildProfileState`) that ignores the just-successful fetch. Child bead: `monitor-row-status-noise`.

## Recorded user decisions (defaults adopted; user may veto)
- **D1**: Live read-only probes with real tokens are allowed (GET only; no logins; token *refresh* is allowed per D2 but only via the existing refresh flow).
- **D2**: Fix shape: **recommended** — monitor may refresh tokens and persist to vault, reusing `internal/refresh.RefreshProfile`. Rationale: it is the only fix that makes the probe truthful; a read-only alternative (display "token stale — run caam refresh" instead of "auth expired") is rejected because it still cannot show usage for healthy accounts. The read-only alternative must remain documented in the child bead in case the user vetoes.
- **D3**: Codex "unknown" WARN rows are in scope (child bead 3).

## Definition of done for the epic
`caam monitor --once` (table and `--format json`) on a machine with 5 healthy Claude profiles and 2 healthy Codex profiles shows real usage bars for every account, with no "auth expired", no "status 429", no "| unknown", and no [WARN] on rows whose fetch succeeded.

## Security constraints (all children)
- Never log/print token values (max first 8 chars + length in debug output).
- Read-only GETs against provider usage APIs; the only writes are vault credential updates performed by the existing `internal/refresh` code paths.
- Never write to live `~/.claude` / `~/.codex` credential files from the monitor.

Label: `required_provider:any`.

beads.title: Monitor probe: refresh expired vault tokens via internal/refresh before declaring auth expired
beads.description_md:
# Bug: monitor reports "auth expired (re-login)" for healthy accounts because vault token copies are stale

Part of epic `monitor-false-errors-epic`. Label: `required_provider:any`.

## Problem
User output (2026-07-03): `[WARN] benson@feta.fund  no usage: auth expired (re-login)` (also cabot, saumil_2) — yet `caam shallow-spawn` for these profiles works and /usage succeeds. The accounts are healthy; the monitor's token source is stale.

## Root cause (file:line evidence)
- `internal/monitor/monitor.go:129 Refresh()` builds a `tokens map[name]token` from `readAccessToken()` at `monitor.go:288-316`, which reads `vault.ProfilePath(provider,name)/.credentials.json` (claude; fallbacks `.claude.json`, `auth.json`) or `auth.json` (codex) via `usage.ReadClaudeCredentials` / `usage.ReadCodexCredentials`.
- No token refresh happens anywhere in the probe. Claude OAuth access tokens are short-lived (hours). Live Claude Code refreshes tokens for the *active* profile only; every non-active profile's vault copy eventually holds an expired access token (with a still-valid refresh token).
- The usage endpoint returns 401/403; `internal/usage/claude.go` maps that to error "unauthorized: token expired or invalid"; `internal/monitor/alerts.go:90-98 shortUsageError()` displays "auth expired (re-login)".
- **Reusable fix machinery already exists**: `internal/refresh/refresh.go:40 RefreshProfile(ctx, provider, profile string, vault *authfile.Vault, store *health.Storage) error` — refreshes claude/codex/gemini tokens using the vault's refresh token, writes updated creds back to the vault (`UpdateClaudeAuth` claude.go:85, `UpdateCodexAuth` codex.go:81), guards against clobbering the live files (`snapshotMatchesProfile` refresh.go:279), validates token endpoints (`url_guard.go`), and surfaces `RefreshTokenReusedError` (errors.go:62) when the refresh token was already rotated elsewhere. Also `ShouldRefresh(h, threshold)` at refresh.go:26.

## Recorded user decision D2 (default adopted; veto point)
**Recommendation (implement this)**: the monitor MAY refresh tokens and persist them to the vault, exclusively through `internal/refresh.RefreshProfile`. Rationale: it is the only way the probe can report truthful usage for non-active profiles; refresh is idempotent and the refresh package already handles rotation races.
**Rejected read-only alternative (document only; fallback if user vetoes)**: detect expiry locally and display "token stale — run `caam refresh <profile>`" instead of "auth expired (re-login)". Rejected because usage would still be unavailable for healthy accounts, defeating the monitor's purpose.

## Fix spec
In `internal/monitor/monitor.go`:
1. Extend the token-collection loop inside `Refresh()` (around monitor.go:167-192):
   - When reading credentials, also read the token expiry (the `ReadClaudeCredentials`/`ReadCodexCredentials` helpers in `internal/usage` return a second value — use/extend it to get `expiresAt`). If the access token is missing, expired, or expires within a small skew window (recommend 2 minutes), call `refresh.RefreshProfile(ctx, provider, name, m.vault, m.health)` once, then re-read the token from the vault.
2. Add a 401-retry path: after `FetchAllProfiles` returns, for each result whose `UsageInfo.Error` indicates unauthorized (match the exact strings produced by `internal/usage/claude.go` and `codex.go`: "unauthorized: token expired or invalid"), attempt exactly ONE `refresh.RefreshProfile` + single re-fetch for that profile. Never loop.
3. Rate-limit refresh attempts: at most one refresh attempt per (provider, profile) per monitor interval; track last-attempt timestamps in the Monitor struct so the 30s loop cannot hammer the token endpoint after a hard failure.
4. Failure semantics: if `RefreshProfile` returns `*refresh.RefreshTokenReusedError` or any error, keep today's behavior (the row shows "auth expired (re-login)") — that is now a TRUE statement. Optionally distinguish "re-login needed (refresh token invalid)".
5. Make refresh behavior injectable for tests (e.g. a `refreshFn func(ctx, provider, name) error` field on Monitor defaulting to the real implementation), consistent with the existing `WithFetcher` option pattern (monitor.go:55).
6. Codex: same logic applies; `refreshCodex` exists at refresh.go:116. Gemini/opencode/cursor: unchanged (readAccessToken already errors for opencode/cursor at monitor.go:311).

## Behavior before/after
- Before: non-active healthy profiles show `no usage: auth expired (re-login)` forever.
- After: first `Refresh()` transparently refreshes stale vault tokens; rows show real usage bars. Only genuinely dead refresh tokens show a re-login message.

## Acceptance criteria
- `caam monitor --once` on a machine with healthy-but-inactive Claude profiles shows real usage percentages for all of them (no "auth expired" rows).
- A profile whose refresh token is truly invalid still shows a re-login hint after exactly one refresh attempt per interval.
- Unit tests pass; no test performs live network calls (use httptest / injected refreshFn).
- No token value is ever logged (max first 8 chars + length in any debug output).
- Monitor never writes to live `~/.claude` / `~/.codex`; vault writes happen only inside `internal/refresh` code paths.

## Test guidance
- `internal/monitor/monitor_test.go`: add cases — (a) expired-expiry credential in a temp vault triggers injected refreshFn exactly once and re-reads the new token; (b) fetch result with error "unauthorized: token expired or invalid" triggers one refresh + one re-fetch, and the second successful fetch's UsageInfo lands in state; (c) refreshFn failure leaves the original error in state and does not retry within the same Refresh(); (d) two consecutive Refresh() calls within the throttle window attempt refresh at most once.
- Reuse existing fake-fetcher patterns already present in monitor tests; extend `internal/usage` credential-reader tests only if you change their signatures.

beads.title: Monitor probe: stop self-inflicted 429s (serialize+space per-provider fetches, honor Retry-After, soften 429 display)
beads.description_md:
# Bug: monitor's burst of concurrent usage requests triggers 429s, shown as scary errors

Part of epic `monitor-false-errors-epic`. Label: `required_provider:any`.

## Problem
User output (2026-07-03): `[WARN] arthur@feta.fund  no usage: API error: status 429` and same for saumil — while the same accounts work fine interactively. These are real 429 responses from `https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage` provoked by the monitor itself.

## Root cause (file:line evidence)
- `internal/usage/multi.go:55-100 MultiProfileFetcher.FetchAllProfiles()` launches one goroutine per profile (`go func(name, token ...)` at multi.go:66) — with 5 Claude profiles that is 5 simultaneous GETs to the same endpoint from one IP.
- `internal/monitor/monitor.go:88` sets a default 30s interval and `Start()` calls `Refresh()` on every tick, so the burst repeats every 30s indefinitely.
- `internal/usage/claude.go Fetch()` maps any non-200/401/403 to error `"API error: status N"`; the Retry-After header is ignored; the row's previous good usage is discarded (each `Refresh()` builds a brand-new `MonitorState`, monitor.go:130).
- Display: `internal/monitor/alerts.go:68 usageUnavailable()` renders `no usage: API error: status 429` and the row gets a WARN indicator.

## Fix spec
Two layers — pacing (primary) and presentation (safety net):

### 1. Pacing in `internal/usage/multi.go`
- In `FetchAllProfiles`, serialize requests per provider (or cap concurrency at 1-2) and space successive requests by a small delay with jitter — recommend 750ms +/- 250ms between requests to the same provider. Providers still run in parallel with each other (the per-provider goroutine fan-out in monitor.go:198-204 is fine). Deterministic profile order (sort names) so tests are stable.
- Respect `ctx` cancellation during spacing sleeps.

### 2. 429 handling in `internal/usage/claude.go` and `codex.go`
- Add a distinct case for `http.StatusTooManyRequests`: set a machine-recognizable error (e.g. `"rate limited"` prefix; add a helper/sentinel in `internal/usage/usage.go`) and parse `Retry-After` (seconds or HTTP-date) into a field on `UsageInfo` (e.g. `RetryAfter time.Duration`). Do NOT retry inside the fetcher.

### 3. State retention + display in `internal/monitor`
- In `Refresh()` (monitor.go:129): when a fetch fails with the rate-limited error AND the previous state (`m.state.Profiles[key]`) holds real usage data (`MostConstrainedWindow() != nil`), carry the previous `UsageInfo` forward into the new state, marking it stale (e.g. keep its original `FetchedAt`). The row then keeps showing the last-known bar.
- In `alerts.go shortUsageError()` (alerts.go:89): add a case mapping the rate-limited error to `"rate limited (retrying)"` — ASCII only (see comment at alerts.go:82 about byte-width padding).
- A 429 row must NOT get a WARN/CRIT indicator by itself (it is transient); coordinate with bead `monitor-row-status-noise` which reworks the indicator.
- Optional (only if trivial): skip fetching a profile whose previous 429 had `Retry-After` later than now.

## Behavior before/after
- Before: 5-way burst every 30s; 429 rows show `no usage: API error: status 429` with WARN and lose their usage bar.
- After: requests are spaced; the endpoint is not provoked; if a 429 still occurs, the row keeps its last-known bar with a calm "rate limited (retrying)" note.

## Acceptance criteria
- With 5 healthy Claude profiles, `caam monitor --once` shows real usage for all of them (no 429 rows) on repeated runs.
- Unit test proves `FetchAllProfiles` never has more than the configured number of in-flight requests per provider (use an httptest server counting concurrent requests).
- A 429 response with `Retry-After: 30` populates `UsageInfo.RetryAfter` and produces the "rate limited" error string.
- A rate-limited profile with prior good usage keeps its bar in the rendered table.
- Security: read-only GETs; never log token values (max first 8 chars + length).
- Recorded decision D1: live read-only probes with real tokens are permitted for manual verification (max ~6 requests, spaced >=2s) — but automated tests must be offline.

## Test guidance
- `internal/usage/multi_test.go` (create if absent): concurrency-cap test with httptest server; context-cancellation during spacing.
- `internal/usage/claude_test.go` / `codex_test.go` (files exist): 429 + Retry-After parsing cases (both integer-seconds and HTTP-date forms).
- `internal/monitor/monitor_test.go`: previous-state retention on rate-limited fetch.
- `internal/monitor/alerts_test.go` (extend existing): `shortUsageError` mapping for the new rate-limited string.

beads.title: Monitor table: remove false 'unknown' pool status and WARN indicator on rows with successful usage
beads.description_md:
# Bug: successful Codex rows render as `[WARN] ... 34% | unknown`

Part of epic `monitor-false-errors-epic`. In scope per recorded user decision **D3**. Label: `required_provider:any`.

## Problem
User output (2026-07-03):
```
CODEX
[WARN] arthur@feta.fund     ######--------------  34% | unknown
[WARN] saumil@feta.fund     ##########----------  54% | unknown
```
The usage bar proves the fetch SUCCEEDED (real 34%/54% from `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage`). Both `[WARN]` and `unknown` are noise unrelated to the fetch.

## Root cause (file:line evidence)
- **"| unknown"**: `internal/monitor/render_table.go:71` — `status := p.PoolStatus.String()`. `PoolStatus` is `authpool.PoolStatusUnknown` for any profile not enrolled in an auth pool (`internal/authpool/pool.go:135-144` returns `PoolStatusUnknown` when the profile is not in the pool; `internal/authpool/status.go:13-14`). Most users never configure a pool, so every row prints "unknown". (`cmd/caam/cmd/monitor.go:129-135` does pass `WithAuthPool(pool)`, but profiles are simply not pool members.)
- **`[WARN]` prefix**: `render_table.go:57` — `healthEmoji(p.Health)`; `p.Health` comes from `buildProfileState` (`internal/monitor/monitor.go:318+`) which reads the health store (`health.CalculateStatus`, `internal/health/status.go:67`) — stale token-expiry timestamps and past error counts there yield Warning even when the fetch just succeeded. The freshly fetched `UsageInfo` is never fed back into the displayed health.

## Fix spec (display-level, minimal lift — do NOT redesign the renderer)
In `internal/monitor/render_table.go` (success branch, lines 66-77):
1. Replace the trailing status when pool status is `PoolStatusUnknown`:
   - If in cooldown: keep the existing `cooldown Xm` text (render_table.go:72-74).
   - Else if the usage window has a reset time: show `resets <compact duration>` using the existing `formatDuration`/`formatCooldown` helpers (render.go:196-230) and `UsageInfo.MostConstrainedWindow().ResetsAt`.
   - Else: empty (omit the `| ...` suffix entirely).
   - Only print a real pool status (`active`, `cooldown`, etc.) when it is not Unknown.
2. Indicator honesty: when the row's `UsageInfo` has real data (`MostConstrainedWindow() != nil || Credits != nil`) and no error, the indicator must reflect the fetch: show `OK` unless the usage-based alert (`p.Alert`, from `evaluateAlert` in alerts.go) is Warning/Critical/Exhausted — in that case show the alert level via the existing `alertEmoji` (render.go:169-180). Health-store status may still drive the indicator for rows WITHOUT fresh usage data. Keep `healthEmoji`/`alertEmoji` as-is; change only which one the row uses.
3. ASCII only — `writeLine` pads by byte length (see comment at alerts.go:82); multi-byte runes break the box border.
4. Apply identically to all providers (Claude rows have the same latent issues once beads `monitor-refresh-stale-tokens` and `monitor-429-pacing` make their fetches succeed).
5. JSON/brief renderers: leave field contents unchanged (JSON already exposes pool_status separately, render.go:60-67); this bead is table-only.

## Behavior before/after
- Before: `[WARN] arthur@feta.fund  ######--------------  34% | unknown`
- After:  `[OK] arthur@feta.fund    ######--------------  34% | resets 2h 10m` (suffix omitted if no reset time; WARN/CRIT/EXH only when usage alert thresholds are actually crossed or the fetch failed).

## Acceptance criteria
- `caam monitor --once` shows no literal `unknown` in any table row and no WARN indicator on any row whose usage fetch succeeded and is below alert thresholds.
- Rows crossing the usage alert threshold still show WARN/CRIT/EXH.
- Pool-enrolled profiles still show their real pool status; cooldown display unchanged.
- Table borders stay aligned (byte-width padding preserved, ASCII only).
- No token values logged.

## Test guidance
- `internal/monitor/render_test.go` / add `render_table_test.go` cases: (a) successful UsageInfo + PoolStatusUnknown + window reset time -> `resets ...` suffix, OK indicator; (b) successful UsageInfo at 96% utilization -> alert-driven CRIT indicator; (c) failed fetch row -> unchanged "no usage: ..." path with health-driven indicator; (d) PoolStatus active -> real status printed; (e) border alignment: every rendered line same byte length.
- Follow existing table-render test patterns in `internal/monitor` (issue #37 tests cover the `usageUnavailable` path — mirror their style).

filing_notes: Verified all root causes directly in the repo (the gatherer evidence sections arrived as unexpanded placeholders, so I re-traced: monitor.go:129/288, usage/multi.go:55-100, render_table.go:57&71, authpool/pool.go:144, refresh/refresh.go:40). File with `br` (beads_rust, ids caam-XXXX): create the epic first, then the three bugs with dep on the epic; add label `required_provider:any` to every bead (schema here has no label field — apply at filing time). Priorities: epic P1, stale-token and 429 beads P1, display-noise bead P2. Suggested execution order: monitor-refresh-stale-tokens and monitor-429-pacing in parallel, monitor-row-status-noise after (it references the softened 429 display). D2 veto point is recorded inside monitor-refresh-stale-tokens (read-only alternative documented). Deliverable 2 (display expansion: weekly+5h windows, Fable / GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark per-model usage with D4 graceful omit) is NOT covered here — it belongs to the deliverable-2 architect; note that internal/usage UsageInfo already carries Primary/Secondary/Tertiary windows, so deliverable 2 should depend on monitor-row-status-noise to avoid renderer merge conflicts.
